entries.claim: The pass-start cache is reused for all of backfill even though backfill itself changes the rows it caches, and the plan's `taken`-map argument only establishes freshness for the walk.
entries.failure_scenario: Backfill starts with no cached row for a session key, archives one path for that key, and later encounters another path with the same key in a subsequent dispatch round. The cache still says the key is unarchived, so `read_existing` cannot see the newly written holder, metadata, or watermark and may process the second path as new instead of issuing the existing key-holder refusal. That can change which transcript is archived or indexed. The plan needs either a backfill-wide uniqueness guarantee enforced by a shared `taken` set, cache updates after apply, or a fresh row read at a boundary where prior rounds may have changed it.

counter_evidence.note: `taken` is created once before the round loop ("Across rounds, not per round") and passed to every dispatch_round. claim (crates/terminus-core/src/ingest/mod.rs:192-210) checks `taken` before the store, so a second path with an already-archived key gets Claim::Same or Claim::Held(key_held) and never reaches read_existing or the cached row. Only keys no earlier round applied read the cache, and no apply has changed those rows. PLAN-2 Task 1 already states this per-run argument.

entries.claim: The split snapshot protocol carries a stale due decision and timestamp beyond the ingest lock without rechecking or preventing concurrent snapshot finishers from writing timestamps out of order.
entries.failure_scenario: Pass A decides a snapshot is due with timestamp A and releases the lock. Before A finishes its snapshot, pass B acquires the ingest lock, also sees the old stamp, decides one is due with later timestamp B, then snapshots and writes B. A subsequently finishes and writes its older timestamp A, regressing `last_snapshot_at`; concurrent `take`/`prune` operations may also race over snapshot names and retention. The next pass can consequently take a snapshot earlier than configured, and one concurrent snapshot can be reduced to a note despite another pass already satisfying the interval. The plan needs an ordering/recheck mechanism for the post-lock snapshot stamp while preserving D-15's requirement not to hold the ingest lock through the copy.

counter_evidence.note: The race is not introduced by the plan. Today roll runs entirely after the lock drops (pass.rs:136-147, 165-244): it reads now and last_snapshot_at, takes the snapshot, then writes the stamp, all outside the ingest lock, so two concurrent passes can already both snapshot and write their stamps out of order. PLAN-2 Task 2 moves only the due decision under the lock and keeps the take and the stamp write after release, as CONTEXT D-15 locks; holding the lock through the copy was rejected there.
